summary: End-to-end testing of TMS Order-to-Cash. Backend: 20/20 pytest tests pass (auth, role enforcement, AWB CRUD with calc, costs with payment_type logic, settle, reconcile/revert, invoice idempotency, mark-paid, P&L). Frontend: all critical UI flows verified across operation+finance roles. One real backend bug found: POST /api/invoices is NOT idempotent on already-Invoiced AWBs — status check fires before existing-invoice check, returning 400 instead of the existing invoice.

minor.issue: Spec requires idempotent behaviour (return existing invoice on repeat call), but route checks status != 'Reconciled' BEFORE checking for existing invoice. Once AWB is 'Invoiced', a 2nd POST returns 400 'Hanya order dengan status Reconciled yang bisa dibuat invoice' instead of returning the existing invoice. Fix: reorder — first lookup existing invoice by awb_id and return it if found, then status guard.
Filter silently ignores malformed month (try/except pass). Consider returning 400 to surface user mistakes.
First lookup lowercases username; second fallback uses raw. Mostly harmless but inconsistent — collapse to single normalized lookup.
allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False — acceptable for Bearer-token-only auth, but CORS_ORIGINS env var is set yet unused.

issues: React Router v6 future-flag warnings spam the console (v7_startTransition, v7_relativeSplatPath). Not user-facing but should be silenced via <BrowserRouter future={{...}}/>.

action_items: Reorder logic in POST /api/invoices: lookup existing invoice first, return it if present; only then enforce status==Reconciled. This delivers the idempotent contract stated in the spec.
Optional: opt-in to React Router v7 future flags to remove console warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~810 lines — single-file is fine for MVP, but plan to split into routers/{auth,orders,costs,invoices,reports}.py before adding more modules.
Hardcoded fallback URL not present (good). All env vars are used via os.environ[...] with explicit KeyError — good practice.
_id is correctly stripped via serialize() helper everywhere — good.
Login route does `db.users.find_one({username: lower})` then `find_one({username: raw})` fallback — small extra DB call; collapse with `$regex` ci-match or normalize at seed+login.
All key data-testids present (calc-total-tariff, calc-tax-amount, calc-grand-total, pnl-* cards). Good test coverage attributes.
seed_data_creation: No new seed; backend lifespan seeds 3 customers, 4 contracts, 5 AWBs (1 each of Open/Open/Reconciled/Invoiced/Paid), 10 costs, 2 invoices.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend & frontend baseline is solid. Only confirmed bug is the /api/invoices idempotency ordering. After fix, just rerun /app/backend/tests/test_tms_backend.py and replace the workaround in TestReconcileFlow.test_reconcile_and_revert_and_invoice (currently accepts either 200 or 400) with a strict 200 assertion + matching invoice_number.
rca_of_the_issue: POST /api/invoices route in server.py lines 638-659: the check `if o['status'] != 'Reconciled': raise 400` executes BEFORE `existing = db.invoices.find_one({awb_id})`. Reproduce: (1) create order as operation; (2) reconcile it; (3) POST /api/invoices → 200 with invoice (AWB now Invoiced); (4) POST /api/invoices again with same awb_id → 400. Mitigation: move the existing-invoice lookup ahead of the status check, or relax the status check to allow Reconciled OR Invoiced when existing is None vs not-None respectively.
